_comment: Retrieval evaluation set for LegalMind. DRAFTED BY CLAUDE, REVIEWED BY MUZI LI.
Every expected citation was verified against the text of C-44 as indexed.
Categories exist so that a change to retrieval can be judged per query type,
not just on an average that hides which kind of question got worse:
paraphrase     - plain language, no statutory vocabulary. Semantic should win.
statutory_term - uses the Act's own terms of art.
section_number - names a provision by number. Embeddings blur these.
definition     - asks for a defined term from s. 2(1).
multi_provision- correct answer needs more than one provision.
'term' narrows a match to one definition chunk, since ~39 chunks share the

cases.question: what happens if a director has a conflict of interest?
what standard of care must directors meet?
can a shareholder sue on behalf of the corporation?
what can I do if the company is treating me unfairly as a minority shareholder?
_note: s. 241(1) is only the procedural hook -- 'a complainant may apply to a court
for an order under this section' -- and contains none of the words a reader
would search for. The grounds ('oppressive', 'unfairly prejudicial') are in
s. 241(2). Retrieving either serves the question.
